subject: Request: geo recovery workflow exception for switchback verification
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasbank.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: geo recovery workflow exception for switchback verification

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking my call earlier. Per our internal change control and regulatory checklist, AtlasBank needs an explicit carveout to the standard multi-region DR switchback expectation. Our compliance team requires an additional verification window after a regional failover to run data residency checks and transaction integrity reconciliation before we allow traffic to be routed back to the original region.

Current ask: allow a 60-minute switchback verification window (i.e., a controlled delay before finalizing failback) where AtlasBank remains on the warmed-standby region and Redwood keeps capacity pinned.

Rationale: many of our systems perform cross-region reconciliation that can take up to ~45 minutes for peak-batch loads; forcing an immediate 15 minute switchback would risk data drift and regulatory exceptions.

Attachments: atlas-drmatrix.pdf (summary of AtlasBank DR matrix and compliance checkpoints)

Can Redwood accept this as a formal carveout to the RTO/RPO section (we expect RTO target during failover to remain 15m, but switchback finalization can be extended to 60m under the carveout)? If so, procurement will ask for contract language and monitoring hooks.

- Michael Torres
Director, Infrastructure Resilience
AtlasBank

From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: geo recovery workflow exception for switchback verification

Michael — thanks for the clear summary and the DRM matrix. We can accommodate a customer-specific switchback verification window, but we need to formalize the scope and operational controls so it doesn't impact other tenants or our latency SLAs. High level notes:

- We agree the failover RTO to warm-standby can stay at ~15 minutes (service availability).
- We can add a 60-minute controlled switchback verification window where traffic remains on the standby region while AtlasBank completes reconciliation. During this window Redwood will: pre-warm the original region, keep pinned capacity, and hold any automated switchback triggers.
- Caveats: cross-region cold caches and model KV-cache rebuilds may increase tail latency on the original region for the first 10-30 minutes after switchback. We'll capture that in the monitoring SLA carveout.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) Marissa (ops) to confirm the runbook and prewarm checklist for AtlasBank.
2) Kimberly (legal) to draft a short SLO carveout clause and redline.
3) Aditya (sales) to coordinate procurement expectations and penalty/measurement language.
4) Schedule a test failover (suggested window 2026-11-30) to validate timings.

I attached the runbook template and will follow up with a term sheet.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: logan.wright@redwood.com, Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasbank.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T13:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: geo recovery workflow exception for switchback verification

Hi team — ops notes and technical mitigations below. I pulled in estimated timings from our staging failovers.

- Failover (active -> standby): RTO ~ 10-15m for service endpoints when autoscaling/pinned pools are available.
- Switchback (standby -> active): two phases:
  1) Controlled verification window (customer checkpoint) — up to 60m as requested; traffic remains on the standby region.
  2) Final switchover and gradual traffic ramp — once verification completes we do a progressive reweighting over ~10-20m to reduce error rates.

Technical caveats:
- KV-cache rebuild: large model KV caches and prefix caches can take 5-25m to reach steady-state depending on request distribution. This is the primary source of tail latency after switchback.
- Cross-region data sync: if AtlasBank has any asynchronous batch reconciliation, we recommend running those reconciliations in the standby region during the verification window to reduce finalization time.
- Monitoring hooks: ops will emit per-route latency p95/p99 and cache-hit ratio metrics to a shared monitoring endpoint during the test.

Mitigations we can implement for AtlasBank to reduce risk:
- Prewarm: run a scheduled prewarm job that primes hot KV keys for the top 20 routes prior to initiating switchback. (See attached prewarm-runbook.md)
- Graceful ramp: implement a weighted traffic ramp with automatic fallback to standby if error budget exceeds threshold during the first 30m after switchback.

I can have the runbook updated and send the final checklist by tomorrow EOD. Agree on the proposed 2026-11-30 test.

— Marissa Cole
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasbank.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlasbank.com
Date: 2026-11-18T08:21:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: geo recovery workflow exception for switchback verification

Logan/Marissa — this all looks reasonable and aligns with what our compliance team expects. A couple of procurement/legal questions so we can close:

1) Penalties: AtlasBank needs the alternate window to be explicit in the SLA with a measurement definition (i.e., what metric constitutes completion of verification, and how we measure the start/end times of the 60-minute verification window).
2) Evidence: we need monitoring hooks and a post-failover report (ops timeline + p95/p99 numbers + cache-hit ratios).
3) Acceptance test: please confirm the scope of the 2026-11-30 test and what success criteria look like.

If Redwood can provide a draft one-page addendum that defines the verification window, measurement points, and the monitoring link, we will route for internal approval. Procurement is copied.

Thanks,
Michael

From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@atlasbank.com>, procurement@atlasbank.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T16:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: geo recovery workflow exception for switchback verification

Michael / AtlasBank procurement — noted. We'll get a concise addendum draft over to you today. Quick answers below and next steps: 

- Measurement definition: verification window starts at the timestamp when Redwood completes the failover stabilization step (ops will publish the "failover_stable" event). The window ends on the timestamp when AtlasBank raises a formal "verification_complete" event (via shared ticket or API). We will capture and persist both timestamps.
- Penalties: we propose a narrow SLA carveout: no uptime SLA credits attributable to the verification window itself, but any failure to meet the agreed-upon verification process (e.g., failure to keep pinned capacity) will be treated as an operational breach subject to standard SLA credits. Kimberly will provide exact wording.
- Evidence: ops will push the post-failover report (timeline + p95/p99 + cache-hit ratio) to the shared Drive link after the test.
- Acceptance test: 2026-11-30 02:00–04:00 UTC. Success = failover within 15m, completion of verification window within 60m, and post-failover p99 latency <= 2.5x baseline for the first 30m after switchback.

Attached: draft SLO term sheet for the carveout (slo-carveout-term-sheet.pdf). Kimberly/legal will redline and I will route the DocuSign link once we have signoff. HubSpot: HS-83421 for tracking.

Action items:
- Kimberly: prepare redline and proposed penalty language.
- Marissa: finalize prewarm checklist and test runbook; schedule ops on-call for 11/30 test.
- Aditya: coordinate procurement/contract timeline.
- Michael: confirm test window and acceptance criteria.

Thanks everyone — we should have a formal addendum in short order.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
